title: What Is a Fajã, and Why Are There Farms at the Foot of Madeira's Cliffs?
description: A fajã is flat land at the foot of a sea cliff, made by a landslide or lava flow. The soil is rich and the air warm, so Madeirans farm them below the cliffs.
heroAlt: View from the Rancho cable car down to the fajã fields and the sea under Cabo Girão
keywords: farms at the bottom of cliffs Madeira

images.prompt: Realistic photograph taken through the glass of the small Rancho cable car cabin as it descends the cliff at Cabo Girão, Madeira, mid-morning. Far below, a narrow flat strip of green terraced fields with vines and fruit trees and a few tiny stone huts at sea level, a grey boulder beach with white surf, and the deep blue Atlantic stretching to the horizon. The steep dark volcanic cliff face drops away on one side. No people in the frame, natural colours, no text.
images.alt: View from the Rancho cable car down to the fajã fields and the sea under Cabo Girão
